title: Injectivity of the reduced coproduct in degree-two coherent cohomology
statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] and let $A\to S$ be a proper smooth commutative group algebraic space of finite presentation [def-trf-algebraic-space] whose geometric fibres are smooth proper geometrically connected group schemes. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; smoothness and finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts. A line module is an $\mathcal O$-module on the small etale site locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O$ [def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ be any affine $S$-scheme and put $B=A\times_ST$, $C=B\times_TB$, with structure maps $f:B\to T$, $q:C\to T$, addition $m:C\to B$ and projections $p_1,p_2:C\to B$. Let $N$ be any $R$-module, with no finiteness or flatness assumption. Define $F=f^*\widetilde N=\mathcal O_B\otimes_RN$ and $G=q^*\widetilde N=\mathcal O_C\otimes_RN$ on the small etale sites. Cohomology means right derived global sections of the underlying additive sheaf. Using the canonical identifications $m^*F=p_1^*F=p_2^*F=G$, the additive map
$$D=m^*-p_1^*-p_2^*:H^2(B,F)\longrightarrow H^2(C,G)$$
is injective. This assertion includes nonreduced and non-Noetherian $T$, all residue characteristics, and the zero module $N$.

proof.text: Smoothness implies flatness on every scheme chart by [lem-pc-smooth-flat], hence $A\to S$ is flat under the chart convention in the statement. The base-change clauses of [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] make $f:B\to T$ flat, proper and of finite presentation, in particular quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply [lem-sfb-abelian-coherent-exterior-base-change] to the given $A/S$ and this arbitrary $T$. Put $V=H^1(B,\mathcal O_B)$ and $H^i=H^i(B,\mathcal O_B)$. It gives $H^0=R$, $V$ finite projective, and cup-product identifications $H^i=\bigwedge^i_RV$; all these cohomology modules are finite projective and vanish in high degrees. Thus the two factors $B,B$ satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-projective-cohomology-coefficient-kunneth].

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-projective-cohomology-coefficient-kunneth] with $X=Y=B$, first with coefficient $R$. It identifies $H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ with $V\oplus V$ via $(u,v)\mapsto p_1^*u+p_2^*v$, and $H^2(C,\mathcal O_C)$ with $H^2\oplus(V\otimes_RV)\oplus H^2$. Let $i_1(b)=(b,0)$ and $i_2(b)=(0,b)$. Since $T$ is affine, [lem-sc-etale-affine-qcoherent] gives $H^1(T,\mathcal O_T)=0$. Consequently pullback by $i_1,i_2$ is the first, respectively second coordinate on $V\oplus V$: the cross terms factor through $T$, while the matching composites are the identity. The group identities $mi_1=mi_2=\mathrm{id}_B$, together with the cited functoriality, therefore imply $m^*v=p_1^*v+p_2^*v$ for every $v\in V$.

proof.text:
Under the degree-two external cup identification of step 2, the projection pullbacks of $u\smile v$ occupy only the first and last summands. Multiplicativity of pullback and the signed multiplication in [lem-sfb-projective-cohomology-coefficient-kunneth] give
$$m^*(u\smile v)=(p_1^*u+p_2^*u)(p_1^*v+p_2^*v).$$
The two cross terms are $p_1^*u\smile p_2^*v-p_1^*v\smile p_2^*u$. Thus the mixed component of $(m^*-p_1^*-p_2^*)(u\smile v)$ is $u\otimes v-v\otimes u$. By [lem-sfb-abelian-coherent-exterior-base-change], $u\smile v$ corresponds to $u\wedge v$. The coefficient comparison $\alpha_{B,N}^2$ and $\kappa_N^2$ of the Kunneth node commute with each of $m,p_1,p_2$, and with addition and subtraction. Hence the mixed component of the map in the item is exactly
$$\delta_N:(\bigwedge^2_RV)\otimes_RN\longrightarrow(V\otimes_RV)\otimes_RN,\qquad(u\wedge v)\otimes n\longmapsto(u\otimes v-v\otimes u)\otimes n.$$
The same $N$ occurs once throughout; no tensor product $N\otimes_RN$ has been substituted.

source.place: I, calculation (3) before Lemma 12.2, printed p.55; signed expansion and arbitrary-module coefficient comparison supplied here

proof.text: It remains to check that the displayed $\delta_N$ is injective. Localize on a finite principal-open cover of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ where the finite locally free module $V$ has an ordered basis $e_1,\ldots,e_g$; the coefficient/localization comparisons of [lem-sfb-projective-cohomology-coefficient-kunneth] justify using these same formulas after localization. In exterior degree two every element is uniquely $\sum_{i<j}(e_i\wedge e_j)\otimes n_{ij}$: the alternating relations remove repeated indices and reorder distinct ones, and the alternating coordinate forms taking $(e_i,e_j)$ to $1$ prove independence. Its image has coefficient $n_{ij}$ at $e_i\otimes e_j$ for $i<j$. Thus a zero image forces every $n_{ij}=0$ over each open, even when $2=0$ and even when $N$ is not flat. Vanishing on the finite cover implies global vanishing: if $z$ vanishes after inverting each covering element $s_i$, then some $s_i^{k_i}$ kills $z$ for each $i$; these powers generate the unit ideal, so $z=0$. If the original $D(z)$ is zero, its mixed component is zero, and the isomorphism $\alpha_{B,N}^2$ and this coordinate test force $z=0$. The empty basis-pair set ($g<2$), the zero module, and the zero ring are included.
